totals.rows_scoped: contract.standards, contract.operations, contract.shapes, contract.invariants, contract.not_exposed, instructions, best_practices across the 8 cap-layer ideal facets named in the task (cap-agent-runtime, cap-capability-packaging, cap-durable-execution, cap-errors, cap-evaluation, cap-human-interaction, cap-idempotency, cap-isolation). definition_of_done, adapters, composes_with, entities and open_questions were off limits per instruction and not touched.

method: Same method as sourcing-2a (kb/ceremonies/42-sourcing-2a.json): for each proposed row, python3 tools/kb.py show plus grep -i over kb/facts.jsonl, kb/target-facts.jsonl, kb/reference-facts.jsonl and kb/research.jsonl, using each skill's own X-<skill>-* lens plus already-cited cross-structure/end-to-end records. This ceremony additionally scoped contract.operations and contract.shapes (sourcing-2a scoped only invariants/not_exposed/instructions/best_practices and left every operation and shape proposed in these skills), because these eight skills could not reach the 30% stick without touching them - operations and shapes together were 40-60% of every skill's proposed rows going in. Per the task's own guidance, operations naming what a governing standard itself defines (an ACP session and prompt turn for cap-agent-runtime, an RFC 9457 problem body for cap-errors, the AG-UI/MCP-elicitation/A2A ask-watch-decide cycle for cap-human-interaction, the IETF idempotency-key draft's claim/conflict semantics for cap-idempotency, the OCI Runtime Spec's declared-resource/egress framing for cap-isolation) were converted: the call name stays acknowledged as this repository's own invention in the row's own text, while the origin flips to sourced only where a verbatim quote from the cited record supports the row's own specific claim about what the operation does or the fields a shape carries, never merely that a related standard exists. cap-durable-execution and cap-evaluation have no governing standard on PASS.md's own row (cap-durable-execution's row explicitly reads 'no standard; see B5'); their operations were converted instead against research records describing the general mechanism a real engine in that class performs (journaling and resuming from where a crash stopped; version-controlled corpora and regression gating against a stored baseline), which the row's own text names as the sourced half distinct from the call name. Two shape classes were deliberately left proposed everywhere even after conversion passes: a 'Worked calls' or 'Worked example' / 'What a failure looks like' instance (a concrete illustrative JSON example folded in from a former *-use file) in every skill, and any row whose only candidate citation was a REF- id (cap-capability-packaging best_practices[4]), because REF- ids are reference-only and validate_skills.py rejects origin=sourced resting solely on one (tools/validate_skills.py:185-186).
quality_note: Every candidate quote was checked as a literal substring of at least one cited record before conversion (research.jsonl records with no text field use the json.dumps(record) fallback validate_skills.py itself uses, so a quote taken from the record's snippet or claim field matches). Deletions followed lever 1 only where a proposed row was found to be a near-verbatim reword of another row already standing in the same skill - most often an invariant's claim restated a second or third time as a not_exposed row, a best_practice, or an instruction whose own why-field pointed back at 'the sibling invariant row above' (cap-durable-execution steps 3 and 4 said this explicitly). No row was deleted for restating a sibling skill, cap-consumption, cap-errors or an xc- skill by name: no such restatement was found among the proposed rows in these eight skills' own text (several sourced rows do restate a sibling by name, e.g. 'cap-errors already owns the failure shape' - those were left as-is, since restating-with-attribution is the composes-by-name pattern the schema wants, not padding). One quote truncated by an intermediate 250-character print during drafting (cap-human-interaction's ask operation) was caught and corrected against the full research record before the row was written. python3 tools/render_skill.py and python3 tools/validate_skills.py --only <skill> were run after every skill (via a locally patched copy of the validator that only fixes a pre-existing, unrelated NameError in check_structure - a missing warns parameter, present on git HEAD before this ceremony touched anything and confirmed present via git stash on cap-errors and cap-agent-runtime - so the real tools/validate_skills.py was read but never edited, per the task's eight-file scope): final result is 0 errors for all 8, and every skill's own warning count and content is byte-identical to its pre-ceremony baseline (verified by checking out each skill's HEAD skill.json, re-validating, and restoring the edited version), so no new restatement or other warning was introduced under any of the 8 skills' own --only name. Two skill.json files (cap-capability-packaging, cap-durable-execution) were transiently reverted mid-ceremony by a bug in this session's own baseline-check helper script (set -e aborting before its restore step ran) and were recovered from a scratch backup before proceeding; both were re-verified against their final edited state afterward.
